descriptions: memcpy writes sig_len bytes into the REE-provided output buffer out, but the only size check is conditional (out_len < sig_len && params[3].value.b == 0); when params[3].value.b != 0, the write can proceed even if out_len < sig_len, enabling an out-of-bounds write into shared memory.

memcpy writes sig_len bytes to the shared output buffer out, but the only short-buffer guard is conditional on params[3].value.b == 0; when b != 0, out_len is not checked against sig_len, so an attacker can supply too-small out_len and still trigger an out-of-bounds write into shared memory.

memcpy writes sig_len bytes to out (REE shared output buffer) but the only size guard is conditional (out_len < sig_len && params[3].value.b == 0); when value.b != 0, the copy can proceed even if out_len < sig_len, causing an out-of-bounds write into shared memory.

memcpy writes sig_len bytes into the REE-provided output buffer (out) but the only size check is conditional (out_len < sig_len && params[3].value.b == 0); when params[3].value.b != 0, there is no guard ensuring out_len >= sig_len, so a REE-controlled too-small buffer can be overflowed.

memcpy(out, sig, sig_len) writes into the REE-provided output buffer without ensuring out_len >= sig_len in the params[3].value.b != 0 case; the earlier short-buffer check is conditional and can be bypassed, so a tainted/insufficient out_len can lead to an out-of-bounds write to shared memory.

memcpy(out, sig, sig_len) writes into params[1].memref.buffer (shared output) but the only size guard is conditional: it checks out_len < sig_len only when params[3].value.b == 0. When value.b != 0, the copy can occur with out_len < sig_len, causing an out-of-bounds write into the shared buffer.
